key_sub: Action and reaction act on different bodies.
body_html:
How to think about it

Newton's first law describes inertia. The second law says the net force equals the rate of change of momentum, F = ma. Impulse FΔt equals the change in momentum, so a longer stopping time means a smaller force. The third law pairs act on different bodies; with no external force, total momentum is conserved.

Limiting friction is μN; kinetic friction is a little less. In a lift accelerating upward the reading is m(g + a). On a curve, friction or banking supplies the centripetal force mv²/r.

Example

10 kg, μ = 0.3. Force to start sliding?

0.3 × 10 × 9.8

Answer: 29.4 N

Example

4 kg gun, 0.02 kg bullet at 400 m/s. Recoil?

0.02 × 400 ÷ 4

Answer: 2 m/s

Common mistakes

  • Thinking action and reaction cancel.
  • Forgetting that friction depends on the normal force, not area.
  • Using mg as the reading in an accelerating lift.

faq.q: Why do we pull our hands back when catching a ball?
faq.a: It increases the time of impact, so the force F = Δp/Δt is smaller.

faq.q: What is the law of conservation of momentum?
faq.a: With no external force, the total momentum of a system stays constant.
